Braket supports a diverse set of hardware from leading providers, including superconducting systems from Rigetti Computing, Oxford Quantum Circuits, neutral atom from QuEra, [ion-trap systems from IonQ](https://thequantuminsider.com/2025/02/21/ionq-develops-assembly-chamber-for-miniaturized-room-temperature-ion-trap-vacuum-packages/), quantum [annealers from D-Wave](https://thequantuminsider.com/2025/03/13/d-wave-deep-dive-a-look-at-the-quantum-advantage-findings-and-the-questions-that-remain/), and [photonic devices from Xanadu](https://thequantuminsider.com/2025/06/05/xanadu-demonstrates-scalable-building-block-for-photonic-quantum-computers/). In 2024, it integrated [Rigetti’s 84-qubit Ankaa-2 processor](https://thequantuminsider.com/2024/08/28/amazon-braket-cloud-computing-platform-announces-rigetti-ankaa-2-superconducting-quantum-processor-for-continuous-access/), the company’s most advanced superconducting quantum system, and introduced the Quantum Embark Program. Their January 2025[Leap Quantum LaunchPad program](https://thequantuminsider.com/2025/01/22/d-wave-announces-new-leap-quantum-launchpad-program-to-support-quantum-computing-applications/) offers startups and researchers a three-month free trial to access their 5,000+ qubit systems, development tools, and expert support , further broadening adoption and application of quantum technology. The company operates the world’s largest fleet of quantum systems for real-world applications through its [Quantum Computation Center in New York](https://thequantuminsider.com/2024/09/26/ibm-expands-quantum-data-center-in-poughkeepsie-new-york-to-advance-algorithm-discovery-globally/). ![Image 21: Quantum Computing inc logo](https://thequantuminsider.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/download-2023-12-11T180725.435-300x39.png). AQT is based in Europe and has emerged as one of the continent’s leading players [in trapped ion hardware innovation](https://thequantuminsider.com/2022/02/19/6-quantum-computing-companies-working-with-trapped-ions/), offering a full-stack quantum solution accessible via the cloud. results.title: With Great Power Comes Great Responsibility: The Role of Software Engineers
results.content: *   [4 Research Roadmap for the Role of a Software Engineer](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#sec-4). The role of Software Engineers[1](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#fn1) changes. Thus, the role of Software Engineers changes and continues to do so ([Figure 1](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#fig1)). Donald Gotterbarn already points out the lack of education for moral responsibility of Software Engineers back in 1995 [[56](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#Bib0056)] and becomes one of the champions in developing the codes of conduct in our field. [[92](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#Bib0092)] investigated studies on the ethical responsibility of Software Engineers. [[71](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#Bib0071)] state despite a sufficient large number of research studies on Software Engineering Codes of Ethics operationalizing and implementing those codes in the daily work practices is quite difficult and not yet solved. In addition, leverage points as defined by Meadows [[97](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#Bib0097)] and applied to Software Engineering by Penzenstadler et al. [[110](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#Bib0110)] can be used to look at the impacts of Software Engineering practices. Scenario analysis could be used to assess dynamic aspects of Software Engineering technologies still under development [[116](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3715112#Bib0116)]. results.title: The 2016 Survey: Algorithm impacts by 2026 | Imagining the Internet
results.content: # The 2016 Survey: Algorithm impacts by 2026. ## Will impacts of the networked, automated world be mostly positive? **Link to Full SurveyExperts and highly engaged netizens participated in answering a five-question survey fielded by the Imagining the Internet Center and the Pew Internet, Science & Technology Project from July 1-August 12, 2016. This report, issued Feb. 8, 2017, is tied to a survey question asking respondents to share their answer to the following query:**. **Link to Full SurveyAmong the key themes emerging from 1,302 respondents’ answers in the report released Feb. 8, 2017 were:** – Algorithms will continue to spread everywhere. – Algorithms don’t have to be perfect; they just have to be better than people. The non-scientific canvassing found that 38% of these particular respondents predicted that the positive impacts of algorithms will outweigh negatives for individuals and society in general, while 37% said negatives will outweigh positives; 25% said the overall impact of algorithms will be about 50-50, positive-negative.
